hypotheses.text: In the definitive clinical summary matrix (Table 1) of Janssen et al. (2022), craniofacial dysmorphisms (HP:0001999) do not conform to an invariant facial gestalt; specifically, individual discrete dysmorphic signs (such as arched eyebrows HP:0002553, epicanthal folds HP:0000286, and thin upper lip vermilion HP:0000219) each occur in fewer than 6 of the 8 assessed individuals (<75%), preventing definitive phenotypic segregation based on any single facial anomaly alone.
hypotheses.rationale: While Janssen et al. (2022) establishes that facial dysmorphisms as a broad category are present in at least 7/8 patients, syndromic diagnosis requires determining whether individual dysmorphic signs have high discriminative penetrance or represent a diffuse non-specific constellation.

evidence.text: Janssen et al. (2022) report eight individuals carrying de novo putative loss-of-function variants in TAF4, identifying common features of intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms, but the exact granular counts for individual facial sub-phenotypes are located in Table 1 / extended clinical tables rather than the main text abstract.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms.

hypotheses.text: In Table 1 of Janssen et al. (2022), muscular hypotonia (HP:0001252) exhibits a significantly higher penetrance (occurring in >=5/8 individuals, >=62.5%) than epileptic seizures (HP:0001250, occurring in <=2/8 individuals, <=25%), establishing that tone deregulation rather than active epileptogenesis is the cardinal neuromuscular feature of TAF4 haploinsufficiency.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior pooled data suggest seizures occur in <25-30% of TAF4-NDD individuals, whereas motor and tone abnormalities are frequent; verifying the exact denominator and numerator tally from Table 1 of the discovery cohort directly tests whether seizure absence can be used as an exclusion criterion.

evidence.text: The discovery cohort defines T4NDD as a monogenic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, behavioral anomalies, and facial dysmorphism across eight individuals with de novo pLoF variants, without designating refractory epilepsy as an obligatory or primary core feature.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms. We propose TAF4 as a novel dominant disease gene for NDD, and coin this novel disorder 'TAF4-related NDD' (T4NDD).

hypotheses.text: Microcephaly (HP:0000252) in Table 1 of Janssen et al. (2022) is itemized in at least 3 of 8 individuals (>=37.5%), whereas macrocephaly (HP:0000256) is absent (0/8), indicating that cranial growth restriction is a directional discriminator for T4NDD against overgrowth-associated intellectual disability syndromes.
hypotheses.rationale: Previous literature notes microcephaly or borderline small head circumference in roughly 30-50% of individuals; verifying whether any macrocephaly is documented in Table 1 establishes cranial circumference directionality as a diagnostic clue.

new_directions.rationale: Eigenhuis et al. (2022) systematically evaluated transcription pause and escape in TAF-opathies and compared TAF4 features with other TFIID subunits in their Table 1, providing a direct cross-syndromic discriminator matrix.
